# PocketPages

> PocketPages v1 is a file-routed, server-rendered page framework built into PocketOne (the `pages` extension): EJS, JSX or Markdown pages in pb_pages/, rendered inside PocketBase's JavaScript VM with a `ctx` API for requests, auth, data and assets.

PocketPages v1 runs in the `pocketone` binary, not Node; PocketPages 0.x (the npm package) is retired, see /docs/moving-from-0x. Agent Skill: https://github.com/pockethost/pocketone/tree/main/agent/skills/pocketpages (Claude Code: `/plugin marketplace add pockethost/pocketone`).

Every page below in one file: https://pocketpages.dev/llms-full.txt

## Introduction

- [Moving from PocketPages 0.x](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/moving-from-0x): What changed between the PocketPages npm package (0.x) and PocketPages v1 in PocketOne.
- [Coding agents](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/agents): Teach Claude Code, Cursor, Codex and other coding agents PocketPages v1 with the pocketpages Agent Skill and llms.txt.

## Getting Started

- [Installation](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/installation): Run PocketPages v1 on PocketOne with the pages extension, using a pb_pages folder.
- [Starter Kits](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/starter-kits): Start a new PocketPages app from a starter kit with pocketone pages create.

## Basics

- [Creating a Page](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/creating-a-page): Create .ejs and .md files in pb_pages to add pages, with index files and nested folders mapping to URLs.
- [Directory Structure](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/directory-structure): How a pb_pages folder is organized, and the special +, _, - and . prefixes.
- [Routing](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/routing): How files in pb_pages map to URLs: pages, [param] segments, groups, API routes, static files, and which route wins.
- [Accessing Parameters](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/parameters): Read route parameters from [param] file and folder names with ctx.params, and query strings with ctx.req.query().
- [Loading Data](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/loading-data): Load data inline in templates or in a +page.js file with load and per-method handlers.
- [API Routes and JSON](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/api-routes): Serve JSON and other non-HTML responses from +api.js files and ctx.res.json.

## Templating

- [EJS](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ejs): The EJS tags PocketPages supports, escaping rules, and what's in scope inside a template.
- [Markdown](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/markdown): .md pages and partials run through EJS, then Markdown, with YAML front matter passed to meta().
- [JSX and TSX](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/jsx): Write pages, layouts, partials and error pages as .jsx or .tsx components, rendered to HTML on the server with no build step.
- [Partials](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/partials): Include reusable templates from _private folders with include(name, locals).
- [Layouts and Slots](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/layouts): Wrap pages with +layout.ejs files, and pass content between pages and layouts with named slots.

## Security and Content

- [Private files](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/private-files): How _private folders hold partials and JS modules for include() and ctx.resolve(), and which names are never routed.
- [Middleware](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/middleware): +middleware.js files run root first for every route below them, with one (ctx, next) signature.
- [Asset Management](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/asset-management): Static files in pb_pages get content-hashed URLs through asset() for long-term caching.
- [Static content](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/static-content): Files in pb_pages that aren't pages or framework files are served as-is, with content types and ETags.
- [Managing Secrets](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/secrets): Read API keys and other secrets from environment variables with ctx.env().

## Configuration

- [+config.js](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/config): Turn on built-in plugins, add JS plugins, and enable debug output from pb_pages/+config.js.
- [Caching](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/caching): How PocketPages caches templates, static files and fingerprinted assets.
- [Errors](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/errors): How PocketPages turns thrown errors into responses, ctx.httpError(), and custom +error and +404 pages.
- [Debugging](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/debugging): Dev mode, debug in +config.js, and logging with ctx.log.
- [Going Live](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/deploying): Deploy a PocketPages app by putting pb_pages next to pb_data on a PocketOne server (pages is built in).

## Plugins

- [Overview](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins): Built-in plugins (auth, realtime) and JS plugins such as the Datastar add-on, turned on in +config.js.
- [Authentication](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins/auth): The built-in auth plugin keeps PocketBase auth in a cookie and adds ctx.session sign-in methods.
- [Datastar](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins/datastar): The Datastar add-on adds ctx.datastar helpers for Datastar script tags, SSE patches and signals.
- [Realtime](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins/realtime): The built-in realtime plugin sends messages to PocketBase realtime subscribers with ctx.realtime.send().
- [Authoring](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/plugins/authoring): Write a JS plugin for PocketPages v1, a factory that returns onRequest, extendContext and transform hooks.

## ctx Reference

- [Overview](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx): Reference for ctx, the one object per request passed to middleware, handlers, templates and plugins.
- [req](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/req): The request - method, URL, query parameters, headers, cookies, body, uploaded files and client IP.
- [res](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/res): The response - status, headers, cookies, redirects with flash messages, JSON, HTML, text, files and server-sent events.
- [data, params, route](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/data): The shared data object, route parameters and the matched route.
- [flash](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/flash): One-time messages carried across a redirect in a cookie.
- [auth](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/auth): The authenticated record for the request, or null.
- [app](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/app): The app - records, collections and settings.
- [pb (JS SDK)](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/pb): Query your app with the PocketBase JS SDK from page code, as the signed-in user.
- [env](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/env): Read environment variables.
- [log](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/log): Write to the app's log with debug, info, warn and error.
- [meta](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/meta): A per-request key/value store for page metadata such as title and description.
- [asset](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/asset): Content-hashed URLs for static files in pb_pages.
- [resolve](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/resolve): Load a module or file from a _private folder.
- [store](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/ctx/store): The app's in-memory store, shared across requests.

## Going Further

- [JavaScript Runtime](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/jsvm): Where page code runs, what it can reach, and using npm packages from pb_pages/node_modules.

## Guides

- [Authentication](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/authentication): Sign users in and out with the auth plugin - passwords, one-time passwords, OAuth2 and anonymous sessions.
- [HTMX Integration](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/htmx): Use HTMX with PocketPages: route organization, HTML fragments without layouts, shared partials, forms, and realtime updates.
- [Realtime Events](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/realtime): Send realtime messages from pages with the realtime plugin, and receive them in the browser with the PocketBase JS SDK.
- [Custom Domains on Fly+Cloudflare](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/speedruns/custom-domain-fly-cloudflare): Step-by-step process to configure DNS records, SSL certificates, and domain verification between Fly.io and Cloudflare. Includes specific settings for A/AAAA records, CNAME verification, and SSL/TLS encryption modes.
- [Google OAuth2](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/speedruns/google-oauth2): Set up Google OAuth2 sign-in for a PocketPages app with the auth plugin.
- [Outgoing Email with Amazon SES](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/speedruns/ses): Step-by-step configuration of AWS Simple Email Service (SES) with Google Suite, including DNS records, DKIM setup, SMTP credentials, and PocketBase integration for production email delivery.
- [Setting up a new email domain in Google Suite](https://pocketpages.dev/docs/speedruns/gs-gmail): Complete walkthrough for configuring email domains in Google Suite, including domain verification, Gmail activation, catch-all email setup, MX record configuration, and sender account integration.
